intro.title: Xinjiang, A Continent Within China
intro.left: Covering roughly one-sixth of China, Xinjiang holds snow mountains, grasslands, deserts, blue lakes, forests, and Silk Road cities within one immense region. The terrain can change completely in a single driving day, while the cultures and food reflect centuries of movement between East and Central Asia.
intro.right: Xinjiang rewards travelers who accept distance rather than fight it. Kanas, Sayram Lake, the Duku Highway, Nalati, Hemu, and Kashgar cannot all be treated like nearby attractions. A strong route follows the season and chooses either northern landscapes, southern Silk Road culture, or enough time to connect both properly.

stay.title: How long to stay
stay.summary: Seven to ten days suit a focused northern circuit; combining north and south needs closer to two weeks.

plans.label: 7 days
plans.summary: Choose one compact northern loop around Sayram Lake, Nalati, and seasonal road access.

plans.label: 10 days
plans.summary: Add Kanas and Hemu with realistic driving days and weather flexibility.

plans.label: 14 days
plans.summary: Connect a northern landscape route with Kashgar and the south by flight instead of adding endless road time.

items.label: Getting there
items.summary: Distances are immense. Most routes combine flights, trains, and long private-car days rather than one city base.

items.label: Getting around
items.summary: Choose either northern or southern Xinjiang unless you have at least two weeks.

items.label: Where to stay
items.summary: Weather varies sharply between mountains, deserts, and evenings. Pack adaptable layers.

items.label: Planning ahead
items.summary: Some border and remote areas have additional access rules; confirm the route before booking transport.
